rationale: Lycopolitan plural of ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ/ⲡⲟⲣⲟ 'king,' here in the form ⲡⲣⲁⲓ̈ with article ⲛ̄-. Parallel to attested Lyc. ⲡⲟⲣⲟ in vocab. Kings as agents of persecution against Mani, paired with magnates (μεγιστᾶνες) and orders (τάγμα).

Idiomatic verbal phrase: ⲣ̄- + ⲡⲁⲧ-ⲟⲧⲟⲩ ('foot/hand-against-them') with ⲛⲉⲙⲏⲓ̈ 'with me.' In hostile context yields 'lay hands beforehand against me, conspire against me.' The kings, magnates, and ranks attempted preemptive action against Mani.

proposed_english: cut away from / reap out from
rationale: Verb ⲟⲩⲱⲥϩ 'reap, cut' + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' Used here of severing Mani from the truth. Preserves agricultural-judicial 'cutting off' semantics.
Lyc. ϣⲛ̄-ⲃⲁⲙ 'find power.' Used in negation: ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩ(ϣ)ⲃⲛⲃⲁⲙ ⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ 'they had no power against me.' Variant ⲃⲛⲃⲁⲙ (line 6) without ϣ may be scribal.
Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲥⲱⲧⲡ 'choose' = 'state of being chosen, election.' Mani 'chose in his power the entire great chosenness' = the elect community. Standard Coptic abstract.
Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲁϣⲁⲓ 'be many' = 'multitude, abundance, numerousness.' Paired with ⲃⲁⲙ 'power' as Mani's two distinguishing attributes: 'how great my power and my multitude.'

proposed_english: none of them either / not at all
rationale: Emphatic negative phrase. Possibly Lyc. ⲗ̄ⲗⲁⲩⲉ-ⲍⲱⲥ ⲁⲛ 'no one likewise either,' reinforcing the preceding negation. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

Possibly Lyc. reflex of Greek ψαλμοί 'psalms' with ⲍ-onset (cf. accumulated ⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ < ζωγραφία, ⲍⲱⲇⲟⲛ < ζῴδιον — pattern of ⲍ for Greek ζ/ψ). 'Great psalms of Wisdom' as Mani's gift to his sons fits the well-documented Manichaean psalm-book tradition. Alternative: from ϩⲱⲗⲙ 'image, form' (cf. Hebrew ṣelem).

ⲛⲁⲍⲣⲁⲃⲁⲟⲥ — etymology unclear. Possibly ⲛⲁ-(C)ⲁⲃⲁⲱⲑ 'those of Sabaoth' (Hebrew/Greek divine name), or a corrupt Greek loanword. Context: gift given by Mani to his sons, paired with 'great psalms of Wisdom.' Flagged for parallel research.

Modifier on †ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ 'this generation' contrasting Mani's age with the 'first apostles' of past ages. Likely qualitative from a root meaning 'leave, abandon' (cf. ⲕⲱ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'leave forth') or 'be lowly, humble.' Translated 'this latter generation.'
Lyc. reflex of ⲣⲙ̄ϩⲉ 'freeman, free person' (cf. ⲧⲉⲗⲉⲩⲑⲉⲣⲓⲁ 'freedom' in same passage). Mani has made his sons, brothers, and kinsmen free from the variety of all works.

From Greek (δι)αφορά 'difference, diversity, variety.' Coptic transcription with elided δι- yields ⲁⲫⲟⲣⲁ. Mani frees his sons from the 'variety of all the works' = the laborious diversity of worldly tasks.
